name: function-docstring
summary: Docstrings on internal functions and classes
explanation:
Flags docstrings on internal functions, methods and classes. Their readers have the source open, where a docstring restates the name and signature and nothing checks that it stays accurate. ## Why is this bad? [PEP 8](https://peps.python.org/pep-0008/#documentation-strings) asks for docstrings on public modules, functions, classes and methods, and for a comment after the `def` line of the rest; the fix writes that comment. Many projects document internal code with docstrings anyway, so this rule is a choice of style rather than common practice. A docstring restates what the name, signature and type annotations already say, and nothing checks that it stays accurate when the code changes. When the reason behind a piece of code is not obvious, a short comment next to that code explains it better. A longer docstring may state a contract the code does not show, such as a tie-break rule, so the fix keeps its text as a comment. ## Example ```python report def load_config(path: Path) -> Config: """Load the config file.""" return Config.from_toml(path.read_text()) ``` Use instead: ```python ok def load_config(path: Path) -> Config: return Config.from_toml(path.read_text()) ``` ## Conflicts with Ruff Ruff's pydocstyle rules ask for the docstrings this rule removes: - [undocumented-public-class](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/undocumented-public-class/) - [undocumented-public-method](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/undocumented-public-method/) - [undocumented-public-function](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/undocumented-public-function/) - [undocumented-magic-method](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/undocumented-magic-method/) - [undocumented-public-nested-class](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/undocumented-public-nested-class/) - [undocumented-public-init](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/undocumented-public-init/) simplint stops with an error before linting while any of them applies to a file this rule checks. Turn them off and let [undocumented-public-api](SMP903.html) ask for documentation on the public API, or turn this rule off. Use [undocumented-public-api](SMP903.html) in place of Ruff's [pydocstyle rules](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/#pydocstyle-d) that ask for docstrings, such as [undocumented-public-function](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/undocumented-public-function/) and [undocumented-public-class](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/undocumented-public-class/): they treat every name without a leading `_` as public, while [undocumented-public-api](SMP903.html) follows `__all__`. When the comment the fix writes gives a Ruff rule a new report, such as [commented-out-code](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/commented-out-code/) for code in the docstring, simplint withdraws the fix and keeps the report. ## What it does Checks for [docstrings](https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-docstring) on internal functions, methods and classes, at any nesting depth. What counts as internal depends on the project. ### Active on - **All code of an application**: an application has no public API, so every function, method and class in it is internal. ```python report def run() -> None: """Run the job.""" print() ``` - **A library's code outside its public API**: whatever [undocumented-public-api](SMP903.html) does not count as public API, at any nesting depth. [undocumented-public-api](SMP903.html) describes how the public API is found. ```toml config [project] name = "demo" [build-system] requires = [] ``` ```python ok file=demo/api.py def fetch() -> None: """Fetch the page.""" ``` ```python report file=demo/_core.py def step() -> None: """Run one step of the job.""" ``` - **Functions in the `case` bodies of a `match` at module or class level**: a `match` that picks an implementation by platform or version is read the way an `if` is, so the functions in each case are checked like the module's others. ```python report file=demo/platform.py import sys match sys.platform: case "win32": def _open() -> None: """Open the file.""" case _: def _open() -> None: """Open the file.""" ``` - **Functions in a private module that other modules import**: a function in a module such as `package/_helpers.py` is still internal when another module imports it, as long as the public modules do not re-export it. ```toml config [project] name = "demo" [build-system] requires = [] ``` ```python report file=demo/_helpers.py def load() -> None: """Load the settings.""" ``` ```python context file=demo/cli.py from demo._helpers import load load() ``` ### Exceptions - **A function an autodoc directive documents**: an `.. automodule::` with `:members:` or an `.. autofunction::` renders its docstring for its users, so the function is public API whatever the project is, and its docstring stays. - **A library's public API**: [undocumented-public-api](SMP903.html) requires it to be documented. That covers what its public modules offer and re-export, and the methods of a public class whose names do not start with `_`. ```toml config [project] name = "demo" [build-system] requires = [] ``` ```python ok file=demo/api.py def fetch() -> None: """Fetch the page.""" ``` - **Public names of a module that an entry point names without an attribute**: a pytest plugin's hooks and fixtures are found by convention, so they are public API and need no docstring. ```toml config [project] name = "demo" entry-points.pytest11.demo = "demo.plugin" [build-system] requires = [] ``` ```python ok file=demo/plugin.py def pytest_addoption(parser: object) -> None: """Register the flag.""" ``` - **Dunder methods, overrides and property setters of a public class**: methods such as `__init__` keep their docstrings, since documentation tools show them. ```toml config [project] name = "demo" [build-system] requires = [] ``` ```python ok file=demo/api.py class Client: """Talk to the service.""" def __init__(self) -> None: """Set up the client.""" ``` - **Names in a module that builds `__all__` dynamically**: every name without a leading `_` is treated as possibly public and skipped, since the module's exports cannot be read. ```python ok __all__ = list(["fetch"]) def fetch() -> None: """Fetch the page.""" ``` - **Docstrings holding a [doctest](https://docs.python.org/3/library/doctest.html) example**: a line starting with `>>>` is a test that `pytest --doctest-modules` runs, so the docstring is data rather than documentation. ```python ok def add(a: int, b: int) -> int: """Add two numbers. >>> add(1, 2) 3 """ return a + b ``` - **Decorated functions and classes**: the decorator receives the docstring and may read `__doc__`, as `click.command` does for help text or `deprecated` does to build its warning. The decorators in the table below are known to leave the docstring unread, so the rule still reports under them. ```python ok @register def run() -> None: """Run the job.""" ``` - **Every docstring of a run in which some file reads docstrings off objects**: through `obj.__doc__`, `getattr(obj, "__doc__")` or a `getdoc` call such as `inspect.getdoc`. A test asserting a function's `__doc__`, or a framework building a schema from endpoint docstrings, may read any of them. A bare `__doc__`, the module's own docstring, does not count. ```python ok file=run.py def run() -> None: """Run the job.""" ``` ```python context file=show.py import inspect from run import run print(inspect.getdoc(run)) ``` ```python report def run() -> None: """Run the job.""" print(__doc__) ``` - **A class whose body reads `__doc__`**: in a class body the bare name is the class's own docstring, so the class keeps it. A method's `__doc__` is the module's, so a method reading it does not count. The decorators, defaults and bases in the header of a method, lambda or nested class run in the class body, so reading `__doc__` there counts too. ```python ok class Sync: """Synchronize the mirror.""" help = __doc__ ``` ```python ok file=header.py class Sync: """Synchronize the mirror.""" def run(self, text=__doc__): return text ``` Decorators known to leave the docstring unread still let the rule report: | Module | Decorators | | ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | builtins | `staticmethod`, `classmethod`, `property` and its `setter`, `getter` and `deleter` | | `abc` | `abstractmethod` | | `typing` | `override`, `overload`, `final`, `no_type_check` | | `functools` | `cache`, `lru_cache`, `cached_property`, `wraps`, `total_ordering` | | `contextlib` | `contextmanager`, `asynccontextmanager` | | `dataclasses` | `dataclass` | | `enum` | `unique` | | `pytest` | `fixture` and the `pytest.mark` decorators | ```mermaid flowchart TD start["docstring on a function,
method or class"] --> api{"public API
of a library?"} api -->|yes| skip["skipped"] api -->|no| doctest{"holds a doctest?"} doctest -->|yes| skip doctest -->|no| decorated{"decorator that
may read it?"} decorated -->|yes| skip decorated -->|no| reads{"run reads
docstrings off objects?"} reads -->|yes| skip reads -->|no| report["reported"] classDef blue fill:#9cc0e3,stroke:#1f4f7d,color:#062d59 classDef yellow fill:#f2d27a,stroke:#6b5410,color:#062d59 classDef green fill:#93cfa9,stroke:#1d5e3a,color:#0b2e1a classDef teal fill:#8ccbc3,stroke:#145c55,color:#072b28 classDef orange fill:#f0b48c,stroke:#8a3d12,color:#3d1606 class start blue class api,doctest,decorated,reads yellow class skip green class report orange ``` ### Fix **Unsafe fix:** code that reads `__doc__` sees the change. That includes [`help()`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#help) and code outside the run: a framework the function is handed to as a value, such as a Starlette route, or a pydantic model whose docstring becomes its schema description. A file with a file-level `ruff: noqa` gets no fix: the docstring's lines may be what its codes silence, and rewriting the docstring would leave them unused. The fix depends on the docstring's length: - A docstring of one line with at most five words, such as `"""Return the value."""` or `"""Helper class."""`, restates the name. The fix **deletes** it with the blank lines after it. ```python report def run() -> None: """Run the job.""" print() ``` ```python fixed def run() -> None: print() ``` - Any longer docstring may state a contract. The fix turns it into a `#` **comment block** in its place. ```python report def _pick(items: list[int]) -> int: """Return the largest item, or the first one on a tie.""" return max(items) ``` ```python fixed def _pick(items: list[int]) -> int: # Return the largest item, or the first one on a tie. return max(items) ``` What the fix does with a reported docstring: - **One line of at most five words**: the fix deletes it. - **Anything longer, when the comment is safe to write**: the fix turns it into a `#` comment. - **Anything longer, when it is not**: no fix is offered. The conditions under which the comment is not safe to write are listed under "No fix is offered" below. The comment text is built this way: - The text is the docstring's source between its quotes, escapes such as `\n` as written, cleaned as [`inspect.cleandoc`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/inspect.html#inspect.cleandoc) gives it: without the quotes, the common indentation, and the blank lines around it, with each line's trailing whitespace dropped. - Blank lines between paragraphs become a lone `#`. ```python report def _fetch(url: str) -> bytes: """Download the resource. The retry count comes from the settings. """ return _download(url) ``` ```python fixed def _fetch(url: str) -> bytes: # Download the resource. # # The retry count comes from the settings. return _download(url) ``` - Lines made only of heading underline characters, such as the `----------` under a numpydoc `Parameters`, are dropped, since as comments they read as section dividers (see [section-comment](SMP001.html)). - Field lists and sections documenting the parameters and results, such as reST `:param name:` and `:return:` fields or the `Args:` and `Returns:` of Google style, the `Parameters` of numpydoc, are left out with their bodies, since the signature documents them. A docstring with nothing else left is deleted, as a one-line one is. ```python report def _run(args: list[str] | None = None) -> int: """ Run the formatter. :param args: command line arguments, by default use sys.argv[1:] :return: exit code - 0 means already formatted correctly, otherwise 1 """ return 0 ``` ```python fixed def _run(args: list[str] | None = None) -> int: # Run the formatter. return 0 ``` - Lines that fit keep their text and relative indentation, so lists and indented blocks keep their shape. - A longer line wraps at spaces. What wraps over joins the next line when that line goes on with the same sentence: it has the same indentation, starts with a lowercase letter, and does not open with a field such as `name:` or `name (int):`. - A URL longer than the room gets a line of its own. - The room is the shorter of Ruff's line length limit and its [`max-doc-length`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/settings/#lint_pycodestyle_max-doc-length), at the indentation `ruff format` gives the body, so the result does not depend on how the code is laid out now. Around the docstring, both fixes do the following: - When the docstring is the whole body, the fix leaves [`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis) as the body, after the comment when there is one. ```python report def _ping() -> None: """Send a probe to the server, then wait for the reply.""" ``` ```python fixed def _ping() -> None: # Send a probe to the server, then wait for the reply. ... ``` - A pragma or tool directive after the docstring, such as `# noqa: E501` or `# fmt: off`, covers the docstring's line only and goes with it, as does a comment holding one anywhere in its text, such as `# first # noqa: E501`. Another comment stays, after the `...` or at the end of the last comment line. ```python report def _run() -> None: """Run the job.""" # noqa: E501 print() ``` ```python fixed def _run() -> None: print() ``` ```python report file=directive.py def _run() -> None: """Run the job.""" # first # noqa: E501 print() ``` ```python fixed file=directive.py def _run() -> None: print() ``` - When other code follows the docstring, a comment after it stays on a line of its own, unless it is a pragma or tool directive, as the deletion keeps it. ```python report def _acquire() -> int: """Take the lock.""" # callers must already hold the registry mutex return 1 ``` ```python fixed def _acquire() -> int: # callers must already hold the registry mutex return 1 ``` - Like the deletion, the comment takes the blank lines after the docstring. - A comment cannot share a line with code before it. The comment for a docstring on the `def` line, or sharing its line with the next statement, goes on lines of its own, and so do the statements after it, as `ruff format` would put them. No fix is offered when: - a comment sits between the docstring and a statement sharing its line; - a comment line would read as a tool directive, such as one starting with `type:`, `noqa`, `fmt:` or `simplint:`, or holding `# noqa` in its text; ```python report def _level() -> int: """type: int, the logging level in use.""" return 1 ``` - a word too long for the room, other than a URL ending the line, would leave a comment line Ruff's [line-too-long](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/line-too-long/) reports, which it skips on a docstring line of a single word; - `ruff format` leaves the docstring alone, under `# fmt: off`, with `# fmt: skip` or in an excluded file, and its indentation is not a multiple of the indent width, which Ruff's [indentation-with-invalid-multiple-comment](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/indentation-with-invalid-multiple-comment/) reports for comments. ## Other tools - **[Ruff](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff):** not requested yet.

name: test-module-docstring
summary: Docstrings on test modules
explanation:
Flags a module docstring in a test module. The module path and the test names already say what is under test, so the
docstring repeats them and goes stale.

## Why is this bad?

The module path and the test function names already say what is under test. The docstring repeats them and goes stale as
tests move between modules.

## Example

```python report file=tests/test_loader.py
"""Tests for the config loader."""

from app.config import load_config


def test_load_config_empty_file(tmp_path: Path) -> None: ...
```

Use instead:

```python ok file=tests/test_loader.py
from app.config import load_config


def test_load_config_empty_file(tmp_path: Path) -> None: ...
```

## Conflicts with Ruff

Ruff's [undocumented-public-module](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/undocumented-public-module/) asks for the
docstring this rule removes, since a test module is public unless its name starts with `_`, and
[undocumented-public-package](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/undocumented-public-package/) does the same for the
`__init__.py` of a test package.

simplint stops with an error before linting while either applies to a test module. Turn them off for test files with
[`per-file-ignores`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/settings/#lint_per-file-ignores), or turn this rule off.

## What it does

Checks for a module docstring in a test module.

### Active on

- **Files named `test_*.py` or `*_test.py`**: pytest's default
  [test discovery](https://docs.pytest.org/en/stable/explanation/goodpractices.html#conventions-for-python-test-discovery)
  names.

  ```python report file=test_loader.py
  """Tests for the config loader."""

  from app.config import load_config


  def test_load_config_empty_file(tmp_path: Path) -> None: ...
  ```

- **Files named
  [`conftest.py`](https://docs.pytest.org/en/stable/reference/fixtures.html#conftest-py-sharing-fixtures-across-multiple-files)**:
  where pytest shares fixtures across the test files of a directory.

  ```python report file=conftest.py
  """Fixtures shared by the tests."""
  ```

- **Any file in a directory named `tests` or `test` below the project root**: the project root is the directory holding
  `pyproject.toml`.

  ```python report file=tests/helpers.py
  """Helpers for the tests."""
  ```

  ```python ok file=app/config.py
  """Load the config file."""
  ```

### Fix

The fix deletes the docstring and the blank lines after it. A docstring that shares its line with the next statement
goes up to that statement. A file with a file-level `ruff: noqa` keeps its docstring: the codes it names may be silenced
by the docstring's own text, and removing the docstring would leave them unused.

**Unsafe fix:** code may read the docstring through `__doc__`: a package under `tests` built as a fixture can use its
docstring as its description.

```python report file=test_loader.py
"""Tests for the config loader."""

from app.config import load_config
```

```python fixed file=test_loader.py
from app.config import load_config
```

```python report file=test_probe.py
"""Tests for the probe."""

import os
```

```python fixed file=test_probe.py
import os
```

A comment after the docstring stays on a line of its own, unless it is a pragma or tool directive, such as `# fmt: off`
or `# noqa: E501`, which goes with the docstring.

```python report file=test_net.py
"""Network tests."""  # these need the staging VPN

import os
```

```python fixed file=test_net.py
# these need the staging VPN
import os
```

No fix is offered when a comment sits between the docstring and a statement sharing its line, or when nothing follows it
but a semicolon.

```python report file=test_empty.py
# fmt: off
"""Tests for the empty file.""";
```

## Other tools

- **[Ruff](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff):** conflicts with released rule
  [D100](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/undocumented-public-module/), which asks for the docstring this rule removes;
  open issue [#10645](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/issues/10645) asks
  [D100](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/undocumented-public-module/) to skip test modules.

name: undocumented-public-api
summary: Public functions, classes, methods and variables without documentation
explanation:
Flags functions, classes, methods and variables of a library's public API that have no documentation. Users read the API through hover help and the generated reference, where the docstring is all they see. ## Why is this bad? Users of a library reach its public API through their editor's hover help and the generated reference, not through the source. A docstring is what they read there: what the function promises, what each parameter means, what it returns and what it raises. Internal code is the opposite case: its readers have the source open, so [function-docstring](SMP901.html) asks for no docstring there. ## Example ```toml config [tool.simplint] project-kind = "library" ``` ```python context file=package/__init__.py from ._client import fetch __all__ = ["fetch"] ``` ```python report file=package/_client.py def fetch(url: str) -> bytes: # package/__init__.py re-exports it return _download(url) ``` Use instead: ```python context file=package/__init__.py from ._client import fetch __all__ = ["fetch"] ``` ```python ok file=package/_client.py def fetch(url: str) -> bytes: """Download the resource at a URL. :param url: Address of the resource. :returns: The response body. """ return _download(url) ``` ## Configuration - [`project-kind`](https://simplint.readthedocs.io/en/latest/configuration/project.html#library-or-application) in `[tool.simplint]`: whether the project is a library or an application ```toml config [tool.simplint] project-kind = "library" ``` ```python context file=demo/__init__.py from demo._core import fetch as fetch ``` ```python report file=demo/_core.py def fetch() -> None: print() ``` - [`api-packages`](https://simplint.readthedocs.io/en/latest/configuration/project.html#api-packages-and-modules) in `[tool.simplint]`: the top-level packages whose modules make up the public API ```toml config [tool.simplint] project-kind = "library" api-packages = ["demo"] ``` ```python context file=demo/__init__.py from demo._api import fetch as fetch ``` ```python report file=demo/_api.py def fetch() -> None: print() ``` ```python ok file=tools/build.py def build() -> None: print() ``` ## What it does Checks that a library's public API is documented. No fix is offered, since only the author knows what the API promises. ### Active on - **Public variables**: each needs a docstring on the line below it, or a `#:` comment on the line above it or at the end of its line, the forms [Sphinx autodoc](https://www.sphinx-doc.org/en/master/usage/extensions/autodoc.html#directive-autoattribute) reads. ```toml config [tool.simplint] project-kind = "library" ``` ```python report file=demo/api.py LIMIT = 10 ``` ```python ok file=demo/limits.py #: The most jobs run at once. LIMIT = 10 RATE = 2 """The jobs started per second.""" ``` - **Type aliases from a `type` statement**: a public alias needs a docstring like any public variable. ```toml config [project] requires-python = ">=3.12" [tool.simplint] project-kind = "library" ``` ```python report file=demo/api.py type Pair = tuple[int, int] ``` - **Definitions in the `case` bodies of a `match` at module or class level**: a `match` that picks an implementation by platform or version is read the way an `if` is, so the definitions in each case of a re-exported private module are the module's too. ```toml config [tool.simplint] project-kind = "library" ``` ```python context file=demo/__init__.py from demo._platform import open_thing as open_thing ``` ```python report file=demo/_platform.py import sys match sys.platform: case "win32": def open_thing() -> int: return 1 case _: def open_thing() -> int: return 2 ``` - **Names a private module defines and a public module re-exports**: the functions, classes and class members of the private module that the public one exports. The report names the module that re-exports the name, so you can see why it counts. ```toml config [tool.simplint] project-kind = "library" ``` ```python report file=demo/_core.py def fetch() -> None: print() ``` ```python context file=demo/__init__.py from demo._core import fetch __all__ = ["fetch"] ``` A re-exported class and its methods are reported the same way: ```toml config [tool.simplint] project-kind = "library" ``` ```python report file=demo/_client.py class Client: """Talk to the service.""" def get(self) -> None: print() ``` ```python context file=demo/__init__.py from demo._client import Client __all__ = ["Client"] ``` ### Exceptions - **Functions, classes and methods a public module defines**: each needs a [docstring](https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-docstring), which Ruff's pydocstyle rules [D101 to D103 and D106](https://www.pydocstyle.org/en/stable/error_codes.html) report. This rule leaves them to Ruff only when the project's Ruff configuration selects the rule for the definition's kind. Ruff's own suppressions of it, through `per-file-ignores` or `noqa`, are respected too. ```toml config [tool.simplint] project-kind = "library" [tool.ruff.lint] select = ["D101", "D102", "D103", "D106"] ``` ```python ok file=demo/api.py def fetch() -> None: print() class Client: pass ``` - **Functions decorated with [`@overload`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.overload)**: the implementation carries the docstring; [function-docstring](SMP901.html) leaves their docstrings alone too. ```toml config [tool.simplint] project-kind = "library" ``` ```python ok file=demo/api.py from typing import overload @overload def load(path: int) -> int: ... ``` - **Dunder methods, such as `__init__`**: the class docstring describes their parameters. ```toml config [tool.simplint] project-kind = "library" ``` ```python ok file=demo/api.py class Client: """Talk to the service.""" def __init__(self) -> None: ... ``` - **Methods decorated with [`@override`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.override)**: documentation tools show the base method's docstring. ```toml config [tool.simplint] project-kind = "library" ``` ```python ok file=demo/api.py from typing import override class Client(Base): """Talk to the service.""" @override def get(self) -> None: ... ``` - **Property setters and deleters**: they share the property's docstring. ```toml config [tool.simplint] project-kind = "library" ``` ```python ok file=demo/api.py class Client: """Talk to the service.""" @name.setter def name(self, value: str) -> None: ... ``` - **Test modules, as defined in [test-class](SMP801.html)**: users never import tests, so nothing in them is public API. ```toml config [tool.simplint] project-kind = "library" ``` ```python ok file=test_api.py def test_fetch() -> None: ... ``` - **Every module of an application**: an application has no Python API. ```python ok def fetch() -> None: print() ``` - **Modules that build `__all__` dynamically**: a module that builds `__all__` with code such as `list(...)` is checked only for the names other modules re-export, because its own exports cannot be read. ```toml config [tool.simplint] project-kind = "library" ``` ```python ok file=demo/api.py __all__ = list(["fetch"]) def fetch() -> None: print() ``` ### The public API The public API is what users of the library can import, following the [typing spec](https://typing.python.org/en/latest/spec/distributing.html#library-interface-public-and-private-symbols) and [PEP 8](https://peps.python.org/pep-0008/#public-and-internal-interfaces): - a module is public when it belongs to one of the library's API packages and no part of its path starts with `_`, so everything under `package/_internal/` or in `package/_core.py` is internal; a dunder module such as `__about__` is public, but `__main__`, which runs as a script, is not; - a public module offers the names its [`__all__`](https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/modules.html#importing-from-a-package) lists, or, without `__all__`, every name it defines without a leading `_`, and the names another module imports from it. A name another module imports but `__all__` leaves out is not offered; [missing-from-all](SMP401.html) adds such a name to `__all__`; - a name a public module re-exports, by listing it in `__all__`, importing it as `from ._core import name as name`, or through `from ._core import *`, is public where it is defined, through any chain of re-exports. A plain `from ._core import name` in a module without `__all__` keeps the name internal. - a class or alias that a listed name's signature refers to, such as a base class of a listed class or an annotation, is public where it is defined, though `__all__` does not list it. This rule requires no docstring for it, while the methods a listed class inherits from it need one, and [function-docstring](SMP901.html) keeps the docstring it has, since the signature makes it library API. - a module that a `[project.entry-points]` value names without `:attribute`, such as a pytest plugin, is loaded whole by its host, which finds its names by convention, so every name it defines or imports without a leading `_` is public wherever the module is and whatever its `__all__` lists. A package it names is its `__init__.py`. ```mermaid flowchart TD name["name in a module"] --> mod{"public module?"} mod -->|yes| offered{"offered by
the module?"} mod -->|no| reexported{"re-exported by
a public module?"} offered -->|yes| public["public"] offered -->|no| reexported reexported -->|yes| public reexported -->|no| internal["internal"] classDef blue fill:#9cc0e3,stroke:#1f4f7d,color:#062d59 classDef yellow fill:#f2d27a,stroke:#6b5410,color:#062d59 classDef green fill:#93cfa9,stroke:#1d5e3a,color:#0b2e1a classDef teal fill:#8ccbc3,stroke:#145c55,color:#072b28 classDef orange fill:#f0b48c,stroke:#8a3d12,color:#3d1606 class name blue class mod,offered,reexported yellow class public orange class internal green ``` ## Other tools - **[Ruff](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff):** variation of released rules [D101](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/undocumented-public-class/), [D102](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/undocumented-public-method/), [D103](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/undocumented-public-function/) and [D106](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/undocumented-public-nested-class/), which cover definitions in public modules and which this rule leaves to them; this rule covers public variables and names re-exported from private modules (variables: open issue [#20766](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/issues/20766)). - [pydocstyle](https://www.pydocstyle.org/en/stable/error_codes.html) reports public functions and methods without a docstring as [D103](https://www.pydocstyle.org/en/stable/error_codes.html) and [D102](https://www.pydocstyle.org/en/stable/error_codes.html). It has no check for variables.

name: long-docstring-paragraph
summary: Docstring paragraphs over the word limit
explanation:
Flags docstring paragraphs longer than 100 words by default, since a paragraph that long usually mixes topics and gets
skimmed.

## Why is this bad?

A docstring is read in the rendered reference and in an editor's hover help, where a long block of text is skimmed. A
paragraph that long usually covers more than one topic; split at a change of topic, each part is easier to find and to
keep accurate. [long-paragraph](SMP002.html) asks the same of comments.

## Example

```python report
def load(path: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Load the manifest at a path.

    Manifests are cached by path and modification time, because parsing them dominates the start-up time of large
    projects. An entry written by one interpreter is not valid for another, since the parsed form depends on the version
    of the grammar, so the cache directory is named after the interpreter. Entries older than thirty days are removed on
    the next run, and a corrupt entry is discarded rather than reported, because the file it came from is still on disk.
    Writes go to a temporary file first, then replace the entry, so a crash never leaves half of one behind. Readers
    never lock, since a replaced file is either the old one or the new one.
    """
    return {}
```

Use instead:

```python ok
def load(path: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Load the manifest at a path.

    Manifests are cached by path and modification time, because parsing them dominates the start-up time of large
    projects. An entry written by one interpreter is not valid for another, so the cache directory is named after it.

    Entries older than thirty days are removed on the next run, and a corrupt entry is discarded rather than reported,
    because the file it came from is still on disk. Writes go to a temporary file first, then replace the entry, so a
    crash never leaves half of one behind.
    """
    return {}
```

## Configuration

- [`max-paragraph-words`](https://simplint.readthedocs.io/en/latest/configuration/rule-settings.html#max-paragraph-words)
  in `[tool.simplint]`: the most words a paragraph may hold, 100 by default, shared with [long-paragraph](SMP002.html)

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  max-paragraph-words = 10
  ```

  ```python report
  def load() -> None:
      """The cache keeps one entry per manifest, keyed by path and modification time."""
  ```

## What it does

No fix is offered, since where to split a paragraph depends on its meaning.

### Active on

- **Docstring paragraphs**: a paragraph is a run of non-blank lines, and it is reported once it passes
  `max-paragraph-words` words. A blank line ends it. Docstrings of modules, classes and functions, methods included, are
  checked.

  ```python report
  """The cache keeps one entry per manifest, keyed by path and modification time, because parsing a manifest dominates
  the start-up time of large projects. An entry written by one interpreter is not valid for another, since the parsed
  form depends on the version of the grammar, so the cache directory is named after the interpreter. Entries older than
  thirty days are removed on the next run, and a corrupt entry is discarded rather than reported, because the file it
  came from is still on disk and can be parsed again. Readers never lock, since a replaced file is either the old one or
  the new one."""
  ```

  ```python ok
  """The cache keeps one entry per manifest, keyed by path and modification time, because parsing a manifest dominates
  the start-up time of large projects. An entry written by one interpreter is not valid for another.

  Entries older than thirty days are removed on the next run, and a corrupt entry is discarded rather than reported,
  because the file it came from is still on disk and can be parsed again."""
  ```

### Exceptions

- **Doctest lines**: a line starting with `>>>` or `...` is code, not prose, so it ends the paragraph before it and
  counts toward none.

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  max-paragraph-words = 10
  ```

  ```python ok
  def double(value: int) -> int:
      """Double a value.

      >>> double(2) + double(3) + double(4) + double(5) + double(6) + double(7)
      54
      """
      return value * 2
  ```

### Report range

The report spans from the paragraph's first line to the line where it passes `max-paragraph-words` words.

## Other tools

- **[Ruff](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff):** not requested yet.

name: rst-field-syntax
summary: Malformed or misplaced reStructuredText docstring fields
explanation:
Flags malformed and misplaced fields in reStructuredText docstrings, such as a misspelled field name or a Google-style
section. Sphinx renders such a field as plain text or prose, so the reference loses the formatted parameter list.

## Why is this bad?

Sphinx renders a field it does not know as a plain field list, and a section from another style as prose, so the
reference shows a misspelled parameter or a Google-style block in place of the formatted parameter list. A duplicate or
misplaced field shows twice or apart from the others. A field spelled with one of Sphinx's aliases, such as `:arg:` for
`:param:`, renders the same, yet a project that mixes spellings reads unevenly and a search for `:param` misses fields.

## Example

```toml config
[tool.simplint]
docstring-style = "rst"
```

```python report
def read(path: str) -> str:
    """Read a file.

    :parm path: Where it is.
    """
```

Use instead:

```python ok
def read(path: str) -> str:
    """Read a file.

    :param path: Where it is.
    """
```

## Configuration

- [`docstring-style`](https://simplint.readthedocs.io/en/latest/configuration/rule-settings.html#docstring-markup) in
  `[tool.simplint]`: `"rst"` turns the rule on

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  def read(path: str) -> str:
      """Read a file.

      :parm path: Where it is.
      """
      return path
  ```

  ```python ok
  def read(path: str) -> str:
      """Read a file.

      :parm path: Where it is.
      """
      return path
  ```

## What it does

Checks the field lists of reStructuredText docstrings, as
[Sphinx's Python domain](https://www.sphinx-doc.org/en/master/usage/domains/python.html#info-field-lists) reads them,
when `docstring-style = "rst"`. No fix is offered for most reports, since the intended field depends on what the author
meant.

### Active on

- **Unknown field names**: a name Sphinx does not know, such as `:parm path:`. The known names are in the table below.

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  def read(path: str) -> str:
      """Read a file.

      :parm path: Where it is.
      """
      return path
  ```

- **Fields missing what they describe**: `:param:` without a name or `:raises:` without an exception, and a `:returns:`,
  `:rtype:`, `:yields:` or `:ytype:` field with a name.

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  def read(path: str) -> str:
      """Read a file.

      :param: Where it is.
      """
      return path
  ```

- **Repeated fields**: a field that repeats an earlier one, such as two `:param path:` fields.

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  def read(path: str) -> str:
      """Read a file.

      :param path: Where it is.
      :param path: Where it is again.
      """
      return path
  ```

- **Aliases of field names**: `:arg path:` and the other spellings in the table below. **Unsafe fix:** the fix renames
  the field to its name in the table and keeps the rest of the line, and code may read the docstring through `__doc__`.

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  def read(path: str) -> str:
      """Read a file.

      :arg path: Where it is.
      """
      return path
  ```

  ```python fixed
  def read(path: str) -> str:
      """Read a file.

      :param path: Where it is.
      """
      return path
  ```

- **Fields after prose**: a field after prose that follows the field list, reported once per docstring.

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  def read(path: str) -> str:
      """Read a file.

      :param path: Where it is.

      Open it in text mode.

      :returns: The text.
      """
      return path
  ```

- **Field lists right under a line of text**: without the blank line, reStructuredText reads the field list as the end
  of that paragraph rather than as a field list. **Unsafe fix:** the fix adds the blank line, and code may read the
  docstring through `__doc__`.

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  def read(path: str) -> str:
      """Read a file.
      :param path: Where it is.
      """
      return path
  ```

  ```python fixed
  def read(path: str) -> str:
      """Read a file.

      :param path: Where it is.
      """
      return path
  ```

- **Sections of other docstring styles**: a Google-style or numpydoc section in an rst docstring is reported.

  - A Google-style section, such as `Args:`

    ```toml config
    [tool.simplint]
    docstring-style = "rst"
    ```

    ```python report
    def read(path: str) -> str:
        """Read a file.

        Args:
            path: Where it is.
        """
        return path
    ```

  - A numpydoc section, such as `Parameters` over a line of dashes

    ```toml config
    [tool.simplint]
    docstring-style = "rst"
    ```

    ```python report
    def read(path: str) -> str:
        """Read a file.

        Parameters
        ----------
        path : str
            Where it is.
        """
        return path
    ```

### Exceptions

- **Two `:raises ValueError:` fields**: they may document two conditions that raise the same exception, so they are not
  repeated fields.

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python ok
  def read(path: str) -> str:
      """Read a file.

      :raises ValueError: When the path is empty.
      :raises ValueError: When the path is not UTF-8.
      """
      return path
  ```

- **A role opening a sentence, such as `` :class:`Path` ``**: a backtick, not a space, follows its `:name:`, so it is
  not a field.

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python ok
  def read(path: str) -> str:
      """:class:`Path` is read here.

      :param path: Where it is.
      """
      return path
  ```

- **The lines of a literal block**: they sit deeper than the docstring's own indentation, so they are not fields.

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python ok
  def read(path: str) -> str:
      """Read a file.

      Example::

          :parm path: Not a field, only text.
      """
      return path
  ```

### What counts as a field

A field is a line at the docstring's own indentation that starts with `:name:` followed by a space or the end of the
line.

The known field names, with the aliases Sphinx also reads and the rule reports:

| Field     | Reported aliases                                                     |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `param`   | `parameter`, `arg`, `argument`, `key`, `keyword`, `kwarg`, `kwparam` |
| `type`    | `paramtype`                                                          |
| `raises`  | `raise`, `except`, `exception`                                       |
| `var`     |                                                                      |
| `ivar`    |                                                                      |
| `cvar`    |                                                                      |
| `vartype` |                                                                      |
| `returns` | `return`                                                             |
| `rtype`   |                                                                      |
| `meta`    |                                                                      |
| `yields`  | `yield`                                                              |
| `ytype`   |                                                                      |

Sphinx renders `var`, `ivar` and `cvar` alike, yet they say different things: `ivar` documents an instance attribute and
`cvar` a class variable, which [rst-attribute-kind](SMP922.html) checks. So none of them counts as an alias of another.

`yields`, its alias `yield` and `ytype` are not Sphinx's own: documentation tools accept them for generators.

## Other tools

- **[Ruff](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff):** open issue [#458](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/issues/458)
  (darglint DAR001, docstrings that do not parse). Open pull request
  [#13286](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/13286) teaches the DOC rules to read Sphinx fields but does not check
  their syntax.

name: rst-inline-markup
summary: Roles without backticks and unclosed inline literals
explanation:
Flags Sphinx roles whose target lacks backticks and inline literals left unclosed in reStructuredText docstrings. Such
markup renders as plain text, or turns the rest of the paragraph into code.

## Why is this bad?

Without backticks a role is plain text: the reference shows `:class:Path` instead of a link. An unclosed inline literal
turns the rest of the paragraph into code, or makes Sphinx warn and show the markup as written.

## Example

```toml config
[tool.simplint]
docstring-style = "rst"
```

```python report
def open_file(path: str) -> None:
    """Open the file at :class:Path, as ``open does."""
```

Use instead:

```python ok
def open_file(path: str) -> None:
    """Open the file at :class:`Path`, as ``open`` does."""
```

## Configuration

- [`docstring-style`](https://simplint.readthedocs.io/en/latest/configuration/rule-settings.html#docstring-markup) in
  `[tool.simplint]`: `"rst"` turns the rule on

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  def open_file(path: str) -> None:
      """Open the file at :class:Path."""
  ```

  ```python ok
  def open_file(path: str) -> None:
      """Open the file at :class:Path."""
  ```

## What it does

Checks reStructuredText docstrings, when `docstring-style = "rst"`, for inline markup that does not render as meant.

### Active on

- **Roles without backticks**: a
  [Sphinx role](https://www.sphinx-doc.org/en/master/usage/domains/python.html#cross-referencing-python-objects), such
  as `:class:`, `:func:`, `:meth:`, `:attr:`, `:mod:`, `:exc:` or `:ref:`, whose target lacks backticks, as
  `:class:Path`. A role's target runs to the next whitespace, without the punctuation that ends a sentence. The fix puts
  the target in backticks. **Unsafe fix:** code may read the docstring through `__doc__`. No fix is offered when the
  target holds a character a reference cannot, as the `=` of `:attr:debug=True`, since where the target ends is then for
  the author to say.

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  def open_file(path: str) -> None:
      """Open the file at :class:Path."""
  ```

  ```python fixed
  def open_file(path: str) -> None:
      """Open the file at :class:`Path`."""
  ```

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  def open_file(path: str) -> None:
      """Open the file at :attr:debug=True."""
  ```

- **Unclosed inline literals**: an inline literal opened with double backticks that no later pair closes within its
  paragraph. No fix is offered, since where it should end is for the author to say.

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  def open_file(path: str) -> None:
      """Open the file, as ``open does."""
  ```

- **Prose directives, such as `.. note::`**: their content is prose, so it is checked.

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  def open_file(path: str) -> None:
      """Open the file.

      .. note:: Use :class:Path here.
      """
  ```

- **A summary ending in `::`**: the lines after it are prose, unless they are indented past the docstring's body. Here
  the line sits at the body's indentation, so its unclosed inline literal is reported.

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  def open_file(path: str) -> None:
      """Open the file::

      Use ``open here.
      """
  ```

### Exceptions

- **Literal blocks indented under a paragraph ending in `::`**: their content is code, which holds no inline markup. The
  first line of a docstring follows its opening quotes, so it is measured against the body's indentation in the lines
  after it, and a summary ending in `::` opens a block only for lines indented past that body.

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python ok
  def open_file(path: str) -> None:
      """Open the file.

      Example::

          x = ``open
      """
  ```

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python ok
  def open_file(path: str) -> None:
      """Open the file::

          handle = ``open(path)

      Close it when done.
      """
  ```

- **The content of a code directive such as `.. code-block::`**: the directive shows code, which holds no inline markup.

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python ok
  def open_file(path: str) -> None:
      """Open the file.

      .. code-block:: python

          x = ``open
      """
  ```

- **Doctest blocks, from a `>>>` line to the next blank line**: they are code, which holds no inline markup.

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python ok
  def open_file(path: str) -> None:
      """Open the file.

      >>> open_file("a") ``b
      """
  ```

- **Docstrings whose escapes make their text differ from the source**: positions in the source hold only for a docstring
  whose text is its source, so the rule does not check them and offers no fix.

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python ok
  def open_file(path: str) -> None:
      """Open the file at \x3aclass:Path."""
  ```

## Other tools

- **[Ruff](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff):** not requested yet. Open issue
  [#283](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/issues/283) names flake8-rst-docstrings only as a plugin candidate.
- [flake8-rst-docstrings](https://github.com/peterjc/flake8-rst-docstrings) reports an inline literal with no closing
  backticks as [RST214](https://github.com/peterjc/flake8-rst-docstrings), with no fix.

name: rst-type-field
summary: Types in docstrings, which belong in annotations
explanation:
Flags type information in reStructuredText docstrings, which belongs in annotations. A type checker verifies an
annotation, while a type in the docstring is checked by nothing and drifts from the code.

## Why is this bad?

An annotation is the type a type checker verifies; a type in the docstring is checked by nothing and drifts from the
code. Sphinx shows annotations itself, in the signature or, with
[`autodoc_typehints = "description"`](https://www.sphinx-doc.org/en/master/usage/extensions/autodoc.html#confval-autodoc_typehints),
in the parameter list.

## Example

```toml config
[tool.simplint]
docstring-style = "rst"
```

```python report
def scale(value, factor):
    """Scale a value.

    :param float value: The value.
    :param factor: The factor.
    :type factor: float
    :rtype: float
    """
```

Use instead:

```python ok
def scale(value: float, factor: float) -> float:
    """Scale a value.

    :param value: The value.
    :param factor: The factor.
    """
```

## Configuration

- [`docstring-style`](https://simplint.readthedocs.io/en/latest/configuration/rule-settings.html#docstring-markup) in
  `[tool.simplint]`: `"rst"` turns the rule on

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  def scale(value: float) -> float:
      """Scale a value.

      :rtype: float
      """
      return value
  ```

## What it does

Checks reStructuredText docstrings, when `docstring-style = "rst"`, for type information.

### Active on

- **`:type name:`, `:rtype:` and `:ytype:` fields**: where the signature already annotates what the field types, the fix
  deletes the field with the lines that continue it.

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  def scale(value: float, factor: float) -> float:
      """Scale a value.

      :param value: The value.
      :type value: float
      :rtype: float
      """
      return value * factor
  ```

  ```python fixed
  def scale(value: float, factor: float) -> float:
      """Scale a value.

      :param value: The value.
      """
      return value * factor
  ```

- **The type in `:param type name:`**: where the signature already annotates the parameter, the fix drops the type from
  the field.

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  def scale(value: float, factor: float) -> float:
      """Scale a value.

      :param float value: The value.
      :param factor: The factor.
      """
      return value * factor
  ```

  ```python fixed
  def scale(value: float, factor: float) -> float:
      """Scale a value.

      :param value: The value.
      :param factor: The factor.
      """
      return value * factor
  ```

  The stars of `*args` and `**kwargs` stay in the name the field gives, and only the type goes.

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  def call(*args: int) -> None:
      r"""Call it.

      :param int \*args: The numbers.
      """
  ```

  ```python fixed
  def call(*args: int) -> None:
      r"""Call it.

      :param \*args: The numbers.
      """
  ```

- **`:vartype name:` fields and the type in `:ivar type name:`**: attribute types are reported but get no fix.

  - A `:vartype name:` field, here for a class attribute

    ```toml config
    [tool.simplint]
    docstring-style = "rst"
    ```

    ```python report
    class Engine:
        """Run jobs.

        :vartype limit: int
        """

        limit = 3
    ```

  - The type in `:ivar type name:`, here for an attribute set in `__init__`

    ```toml config
    [tool.simplint]
    docstring-style = "rst"
    ```

    ```python report
    class Engine:
        """Run jobs.

        :ivar int state: What it is doing.
        """

        def __init__(self) -> None:
            self.state = "idle"
    ```

### Fix

**Unsafe fix:** code may read the docstring through `__doc__`.

No fix is offered:

- without the annotation, since the docstring's type, such as `list of str`, may not be a valid annotation

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  def join(values):
      """Join the strings.

      :param list of str values: The values.
      """
      return "".join(values)
  ```

- for attribute types

- when escapes in the docstring make its text differ from the source

## Other tools

- **[Ruff](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff):** open issues [#12434](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/issues/12434)
  and [#9070](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/issues/9070).

name: rst-restating-field
summary: Field descriptions that only repeat the name
explanation:
Flags `:param:`, `:ivar:`, `:cvar:` and `:var:` fields in reStructuredText docstrings whose description only repeats the
name, as `:param user_id: The user ID.`. Such a description tells readers nothing the signature does not.

## Why is this bad?

Such a description takes the space of a useful one while telling readers nothing the signature does not: not the unit,
the accepted range, what `None` means, or how the value is used. It is often what fills a field added only to satisfy a
check.

## Example

```toml config
[tool.simplint]
docstring-style = "rst"
```

```python report
def fetch(url: str, timeout: float) -> bytes:
    """Download a resource.

    :param url: The URL.
    :param timeout: The timeout.
    """
```

Use instead:

```python ok
def fetch(url: str, timeout: float) -> bytes:
    """Download a resource.

    :param url: Address of the resource, with its scheme.
    :param timeout: Seconds to wait for the first byte.
    """
```

## Configuration

- [`docstring-style`](https://simplint.readthedocs.io/en/latest/configuration/rule-settings.html#docstring-markup) in
  `[tool.simplint]`: `"rst"` turns the rule on

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  def fetch(url: str) -> bytes:
      """Download a resource.

      :param url: The URL.
      """
      return b""
  ```

## What it does

Checks reStructuredText docstrings, when `docstring-style = "rst"`, for field descriptions that only repeat the name. No
fix is offered, since only the author knows what the value means.

### Active on

- **`:param:` fields**: reported when every word of the description, beyond articles and words such as "parameter" or
  "value", is a word of the parameter's name.

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  def fetch(url: str, timeout: float) -> bytes:
      """Download a resource.

      :param url: The URL.
      :param timeout: The timeout.
      """
      return b""
  ```

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python ok
  def fetch(url: str, timeout: float) -> bytes:
      """Download a resource.

      :param url: Address of the resource, with its scheme.
      :param timeout: Seconds to wait for the first byte.
      """
      return b""
  ```

- **`:ivar:`, `:cvar:` and `:var:` fields**: reported the same way for the attribute's name.

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  class Engine:
      """Run jobs.

      :ivar limit: The limit.
      """

      def __init__(self, limit: int) -> None:
          self.limit = limit
  ```

## Other tools

- **[Ruff](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff):** not requested yet.

name: rst-empty-field
summary: Fields with no description
explanation:
Flags `:param:`, `:raises:`, `:returns:`, `:yields:` and `:var:` fields in reStructuredText docstrings that have nothing
after their name, such as `:param path:` with no description.

## Why is this bad?

A field with no description names what it documents and says nothing about it, which the signature already shows. Sphinx
renders the entry with a blank description, so the reference lists the parameter without saying what it is for.

## Example

```toml config
[tool.simplint]
docstring-style = "rst"
```

```python report
def read(path: str) -> str:
    """Read a file.

    :param path:
    """
    return path
```

Use instead:

```python ok
def read(path: str) -> str:
    """Read a file.

    :param path: Where it is.
    """
    return path
```

## Configuration

- [`docstring-style`](https://simplint.readthedocs.io/en/latest/configuration/rule-settings.html#docstring-markup) in
  `[tool.simplint]`: `"rst"` turns the rule on

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  def read(path: str) -> str:
      """Read a file.

      :param path:
      """
      return path
  ```

## What it does

Checks the field lists of reStructuredText docstrings, when `docstring-style = "rst"`, for fields with nothing after
their name. No fix is offered, since only the author knows what the field should say.

### Active on

- **Fields with no description**: a `:param:`, `:raises:`, `:returns:`, `:yields:` or `:var:` field with nothing after
  the name.

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  def read(path: str) -> str:
      """Read a file.

      :param path:
      """
      return path
  ```

### Exceptions

- **Malformed fields**: a field that [rst-field-syntax](SMP910.html) reports, such as an unnamed `:param:`, is left to
  it, since the field must be fixed before its description can be judged.

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python ok
  def read(path: str) -> str:
      """Read a file.

      :param:
      """
      return path
  ```

## Other tools

- **[Ruff](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff):** variation of released rule
  [D417](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/undocumented-param/), which reads Google and NumPy sections only, not reST
  fields; open issues [#458](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/issues/458) and
  [#14494](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/issues/14494).

    :param:
    """
    return path

name: rst-private-field
summary: Public docstrings documenting internal names
explanation:
Flags fields in public API docstrings that document a parameter or attribute named with a leading underscore. The
underscore marks the name as internal, so documenting it in the public reference invites users to depend on it.

## Why is this bad?

A leading underscore marks a name as internal
([PEP 8](https://peps.python.org/pep-0008/#public-and-internal-interfaces)), so documenting it in the public reference
invites users to depend on it. [rst-missing-param](SMP916.html) does not ask for such parameters, and
[rst-missing-attribute](SMP920.html) does not ask for such attributes.

## Example

```toml config
[tool.simplint]
docstring-style = "rst"
project-kind = "library"
```

```python report
def fetch(url: str, _retries: int = 3) -> bytes:
    """Download a resource.

    :param url: Address of the resource.
    :param _retries: How often to retry, for the test suite.
    """
```

Use instead:

```python ok
def fetch(url: str, _retries: int = 3) -> bytes:
    """Download a resource.

    :param url: Address of the resource.
    """
```

## Configuration

- [`docstring-style`](https://simplint.readthedocs.io/en/latest/configuration/rule-settings.html#docstring-markup) in
  `[tool.simplint]`: `"rst"` turns the rule on

  ```toml config
  [project]
  name = "demo"

  [build-system]
  requires = []

  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  def fetch(_retries: int) -> None:
      """Download a resource.

      :param _retries: How often to retry.
      """
  ```

## What it does

Checks the docstrings of a library's public API (see [undocumented-public-api](SMP903.html)), when
`docstring-style = "rst"`, for fields naming a parameter or attribute with a leading underscore.

### Active on

- **`:param:`, `:type:`, `:ivar:`, `:cvar:`, `:var:` and `:vartype:` fields in public API docstrings**: reported when
  the name they document starts with `_`.

  ```toml config
  [project]
  name = "demo"

  [build-system]
  requires = []

  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  def fetch(url: str, _retries: int) -> bytes:
      """Download a resource.

      :param url: Address of the resource.
      :param _retries: How often to retry.
      """
      return b""
  ```

- **The `__init__` docstring of a public class**: it documents the constructor as the class docstring may, so its fields
  are checked too.

  ```toml config
  [project]
  name = "demo"

  [build-system]
  requires = []

  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  class Client:
      """Talk to the service.

      :param url: Address of the service.
      """

      def __init__(self, url: str, _timeout: float) -> None:
          """Set up the client.

          :param _timeout: Seconds to wait.
          """
  ```

### Exceptions

- **Dunder names, such as `__wrapped__`**: a name with double leading and trailing underscores is one of Python's
  special names ([PEP 8](https://peps.python.org/pep-0008/#descriptive-naming-styles)) rather than an internal one, so
  it counts as public.

  ```toml config
  [project]
  name = "demo"

  [build-system]
  requires = []

  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python ok
  def wrap(__wrapped__: int) -> int:
      """Wrap a value.

      :param __wrapped__: The value.
      """
      return __wrapped__
  ```

- **Parameters named with two leading underscores, such as `__obj`**: by the
  [typeshed convention](https://typing.python.org/en/latest/spec/historical.html#positional-only-parameters) the double
  underscore marks the parameter positional-only, so it counts as public.

  ```toml config
  [project]
  name = "demo"

  [build-system]
  requires = []

  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python ok
  def wrap(__obj: int) -> int:
      """Wrap a value.

      :param __obj: The value.
      """
      return __obj
  ```

### Fix

The fix deletes the field with the lines that continue it.

**Unsafe fix:** code may read the docstring through `__doc__`.

```toml config
[project]
name = "demo"

[build-system]
requires = []

[tool.simplint]
docstring-style = "rst"
```

```python report
def fetch(url: str, _retries: int) -> bytes:
    """Download a resource.

    :param url: Address of the resource.
    :param _retries: How often to retry.
    """
    return b""
```

```python fixed
def fetch(url: str, _retries: int) -> bytes:
    """Download a resource.

    :param url: Address of the resource.
    """
    return b""
```

No fix is offered when escapes in the docstring make its text differ from the source.

## Other tools

- **[Ruff](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff):** open issue [#970](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/issues/970).

name: rst-missing-param
summary: Public API docstrings that leave a parameter undocumented
explanation:
Flags parameters that a public API docstring leaves without a `:param name:` field, when the project uses
reStructuredText docstrings. Without the field, the reference shows only the parameter's name and type.

## Why is this bad?

Users read a parameter's meaning in the rendered reference or their editor's hover help. A parameter the docstring skips
shows with its name and type only, leaving its units, defaults and constraints unsaid.

## Example

```toml config
[tool.simplint]
docstring-style = "rst"
project-kind = "library"
```

```python report
def copy(source: str, target: str) -> None:
    """Copy a file.

    :param source: Where from.
    """
```

Use instead:

```python ok
def copy(source: str, target: str) -> None:
    """Copy a file.

    :param source: Where from.
    :param target: Where to.
    """
```

## Configuration

- [`docstring-style`](https://simplint.readthedocs.io/en/latest/configuration/rule-settings.html#docstring-markup) in
  `[tool.simplint]`: `"rst"` turns the rule on

  ```toml config
  [project]
  name = "demo"

  [build-system]
  requires = []

  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  def copy(source: str, target: str) -> None:
      """Copy a file.

      :param source: Where from.
      """
  ```

## What it does

Checks the docstrings of a library's public API (see [undocumented-public-api](SMP903.html)), when
`docstring-style = "rst"`, for parameters without a `:param name:` field.

No fix is offered: the description is for the author to write, and [rst-empty-field](SMP914.html) reports the empty
field until they do.

### Active on

- **Parameters of public functions and methods**: each needs a `:param name:` field.

  ```toml config
  [project]
  name = "demo"

  [build-system]
  requires = []

  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  def copy(source: str, target: str) -> None:
      """Copy a file.

      :param source: Where from.
      """
  ```

- **Constructor parameters of a public class**: they may be documented in the class docstring or in its `__init__`
  docstring.

  ```toml config
  [project]
  name = "demo"

  [build-system]
  requires = []

  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  class Reader:
      """Read files.

      :param source: Where to read from.
      """

      def __init__(self, source: str, encoding: str) -> None:
          """Set up."""
  ```

- **Fields of an attrs class**: attrs names the constructor parameter of a private field without its leading underscore,
  or by its `alias`, so the docstring documents that name.

  ```toml config
  [project]
  name = "demo"

  [build-system]
  requires = []

  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  from attrs import define


  @define
  class Point:
      """A point on the horizontal axis."""

      _x: int
  ```

- **`*args` and `**kwargs`**: they count as `args` and `kwargs`, written with or without their stars, as
  `:param \*args:`.

  ```toml config
  [project]
  name = "demo"

  [build-system]
  requires = []

  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  def copy(source: str, *args: str, **kwargs: str) -> None:
      """Copy a file.

      :param source: Where from.
      """
  ```

- **Parameters named with two leading underscores, such as `__obj`**: the double underscore marks the parameter
  positional-only rather than internal, so it is checked.

  ```toml config
  [project]
  name = "demo"

  [build-system]
  requires = []

  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  def wrap(__obj: int) -> int:
      """Wrap a value."""
      return __obj
  ```

### Exceptions

- **The instance or class a method receives first**: callers do not pass it, so there is nothing to document.

  ```toml config
  [project]
  name = "demo"

  [build-system]
  requires = []

  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python ok
  class Reader:
      """Read files."""

      def read(self, size: int) -> str:
          """Read the file.

          :param size: Bytes to read.
          """
          return ""
  ```

- **Parameters named with one leading underscore**: they are internal, a knob the documentation leaves out;
  [rst-private-field](SMP915.html) reports documentation of them in the public API.

  ```toml config
  [project]
  name = "demo"

  [build-system]
  requires = []

  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python ok
  def fetch(url: str, _retries: int = 3) -> bytes:
      """Download a resource.

      :param url: Address of the resource.
      """
      return b""
  ```

- **Docstrings outside the public API**: [function-docstring](SMP901.html) asks for no docstring there.

  ```toml config
  [project]
  name = "demo"

  [build-system]
  requires = []

  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python ok file=demo/_core.py
  def copy(source: str, target: str) -> None:
      """Copy a file.

      :param source: Where from.
      """
  ```

- **Class variables of a generated class**: a `ClassVar` field is no constructor parameter, whether its annotation is
  written as `ClassVar[int]` or as the quoted string `"ClassVar[int]"`.

  ```toml config
  [project]
  name = "demo"

  [build-system]
  requires = []

  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python ok
  from dataclasses import dataclass
  from typing import ClassVar


  @dataclass
  class Reader:
      """Read files.

      :param source: Where to read from.
      """

      source: str
      count: "ClassVar[int]" = 0
  ```

## Other tools

- **[Ruff](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff):** open issues [#12434](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/issues/12434)
  (DOC101) and [#6606](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/issues/6606) (Sphinx style). Released rule
  [D417](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/undocumented-param/) and open pull request
  [#21076](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/21076) check only Google and NumPy sections, not `:param` fields.
- [pydoclint](https://github.com/jsh9/pydoclint) reports a docstring with fewer parameters than the signature as
  [DOC101](https://jsh9.github.io/pydoclint/violation_codes.html), with no fix.
- [darglint](https://github.com/terrencepreilly/darglint) reports a missing parameter as
  [DAR101](https://github.com/terrencepreilly/darglint), with no fix.

name: rst-unknown-param
summary: `:param:` and `:type:` fields for parameters the signature lacks
explanation:
Flags `:param name:` and `:type name:` fields in reStructuredText docstrings that name a parameter the signature does
not take. Such a field, often left behind by a rename or removal, documents a call that no longer works.

## Why is this bad?

A field for a parameter that is gone, often renamed or removed in a later change, documents a call that no longer works.

## Example

```toml config
[tool.simplint]
docstring-style = "rst"
```

```python report
def load(path: str) -> str:
    """Load a file.

    :param path: Where it is.
    :param mode: How to open it.
    """
```

Use instead:

```python ok
def load(path: str) -> str:
    """Load a file.

    :param path: Where it is.
    """
```

## Configuration

- [`docstring-style`](https://simplint.readthedocs.io/en/latest/configuration/rule-settings.html#docstring-markup) in
  `[tool.simplint]`: `"rst"` turns the rule on

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  def load(path: str) -> str:
      """Load a file.

      :param path: Where it is.
      :param mode: How to open it.
      """
      return path
  ```

## What it does

Checks reStructuredText docstrings, when `docstring-style = "rst"`, for `:param name:` and `:type name:` fields naming a
parameter the signature does not take.

### Active on

- **Function and method docstrings**: fields are matched against the signature. The instance or class a method receives
  first does not count as a parameter.

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  def load(path: str) -> str:
      """Load a file.

      :param path: Where it is.
      :param mode: How to open it.
      """
      return path
  ```

  ```python fixed
  def load(path: str) -> str:
      """Load a file.

      :param path: Where it is.
      """
      return path
  ```

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  class Reader:
      """Read files."""

      def read(self, size: int) -> str:
          """Read the file.

          :param self: The reader.
          :param size: Bytes to read.
          """
          return ""
  ```

- **Class docstrings**: a class's docstring documents the parameters of its `__init__`, or of the fields a dataclass or
  attrs class turns into them.

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  class Reader:
      """Read files.

      :param source: Where to read from.
      :param mode: How to open it.
      """

      def __init__(self, source: str) -> None:
          self.source = source
  ```

- **Fields of an attrs class**: attrs names the parameter of a private field without its leading underscore, or by its
  `alias`, so `_x` takes `x`.

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python ok file=point.py
  from attrs import define


  @define
  class Point:
      """A point on the horizontal axis.

      :param x: Where it sits.
      """

      _x: int
  ```

  ```python report file=alias.py
  from attrs import define, field


  @define
  class Point:
      """A point on the horizontal axis.

      :param x: Where it sits.
      """

      _x: int = field(alias="pos")
  ```

### Exceptions

- **A class that takes its constructor from a base class**: the base's signature is not in the class, so its parameters
  are not known.

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python ok
  class Reader(Base):
      """Read files.

      :param mode: How to open it.
      """
  ```

- **An attrs class with a field whose `alias` is not a string literal**: the alias names the parameter, and simplint
  does not evaluate it, so the class's parameters are not known.

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python ok
  from attrs import define, field

  POS = "pos"


  @define
  class Point:
      """A point on the horizontal axis.

      :param pos: Where it sits.
      """

      _x: int = field(alias=POS)
  ```

- **A function with `**kwargs`**: it takes any keyword, which such fields may document.

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python ok
  def load(path: str, **kwargs: str) -> str:
      """Load a file.

      :param path: Where it is.
      :param mode: How to open it.
      """
      return path
  ```

### Fix

The fix deletes the field with the lines that continue it.

**Unsafe fix:** code may read the docstring through `__doc__`.

```toml config
[tool.simplint]
docstring-style = "rst"
```

```python report
def load(path: str) -> str:
    """Load a file.

    :param path: Where it is.
    :param mode: How to open it.
    """
    return path
```

```python fixed
def load(path: str) -> str:
    """Load a file.

    :param path: Where it is.
    """
    return path
```

When the text left before the field ends in a quote or a backslash, the closing quotes go on a line of their own, since
on the same line they would end or escape the string.

```toml config
[tool.simplint]
docstring-style = "rst"
```

```python report
# fmt: off
def load(path: str) -> str:
    """Load "path"

    :param mode: How to open it.
    """
    return path
# fmt: on
```

```python fixed
# fmt: off
def load(path: str) -> str:
    """Load "path"
    """
    return path
# fmt: on
```

```toml config
[tool.simplint]
docstring-style = "rst"
```

```python report
def split(text: str) -> list[str]:
    r"""Split on \

    :param sep: Where to cut.
    """
    return text.split()
```

```python fixed
def split(text: str) -> list[str]:
    r"""Split on \
    """
    return text.split()
```

No fix is offered when escapes in the docstring make its text differ from the source.

## Other tools

- **[Ruff](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff):** variation of preview rule
  [DOC102](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/docstring-extraneous-parameter/), which checks Google and NumPy sections
  but not reST fields; open pull request [#13286](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/13286) would add them.
- [pydoclint](https://github.com/jsh9/pydoclint) reports a docstring with more parameters than the signature as
  [DOC102](https://jsh9.github.io/pydoclint/violation_codes.html), with no fix.
- [darglint](https://github.com/terrencepreilly/darglint) reports a docstring parameter the signature lacks as
  [DAR102](https://github.com/terrencepreilly/darglint), with no fix.
