name: rst-duplicate-param
summary: Constructor parameters documented in both the class and `__init__` docstrings
explanation:
Flags a constructor parameter documented by a `:param name:` field in both the class docstring and the `__init__`
docstring. Sphinx shows the class docstring by default, so the two copies drift apart as each is edited on its own.

## Why is this bad?

[autodoc](https://www.sphinx-doc.org/en/master/usage/extensions/autodoc.html#confval-autoclass_content) shows the class
docstring by default, so the copy in `__init__` is read by those who open the source only, and the two drift apart as
each is edited on its own.

## Example

```toml config
[tool.simplint]
docstring-style = "rst"
```

```python report
class Reader:
    """Read files.

    :param source: Where to read from.
    """

    def __init__(self, source: str) -> None:
        """Set up.

        :param source: The path to read.
        """
```

Use instead:

```python ok
class Reader:
    """Read files.

    :param source: Where to read from.
    """

    def __init__(self, source: str) -> None:
        """Set up."""
```

## Configuration

- [`docstring-style`](https://simplint.readthedocs.io/en/latest/configuration/rule-settings.html#docstring-markup) in
  `[tool.simplint]`: `"rst"` turns the rule on

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  class Reader:
      """Read files.

      :param source: Where to read from.
      """

      def __init__(self, source: str) -> None:
          """Set up.

          :param source: The path to read.
          """
  ```

## What it does

Checks classes, when `docstring-style = "rst"`, for constructor parameters documented twice.

### Active on

- **`:param name:` fields in the `__init__` docstring**: reported when the class docstring also has a `:param name:`
  field for the same constructor parameter.

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  class Reader:
      """Read files.

      :param source: Where to read from.
      """

      def __init__(self, source: str) -> None:
          """Set up.

          :param source: The path to read.
          """
  ```

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python ok
  class Reader:
      """Read files.

      :param source: Where to read from.
      """

      def __init__(self, source: str, mode: str) -> None:
          """Set up.

          :param mode: How to open it.
          """
  ```

### Fix

The fix deletes the field from the `__init__` docstring, with the lines that continue it.

**Unsafe fix:** code may read the docstring through `__doc__`, and the `__init__` text may hold details the class
docstring lacks.

```toml config
[tool.simplint]
docstring-style = "rst"
```

```python report
class Reader:
    """Read files.

    :param source: Where to read from.
    """

    def __init__(self, source: str) -> None:
        """Set up.

        :param source: The path to read.
        """
```

```python fixed
class Reader:
    """Read files.

    :param source: Where to read from.
    """

    def __init__(self, source: str) -> None:
        """Set up."""
```

No fix is offered when escapes in the docstring make its text differ from the source.

## Other tools

- **[Ruff](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff):** not requested yet. Open pull request
  [#23081](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/23081) (DOC304) reports any parameters section in a Google or NumPy
  class docstring; this rule reports reST `:param:` fields documented in both the class and `__init__`.
- [pydoclint](https://github.com/jsh9/pydoclint) reports any `__init__` docstring as
  [DOC301](https://jsh9.github.io/pydoclint/violation_codes.html), not only the parameters documented in both places.

name: rst-param-order
summary: `:param:` fields out of the signature's order
explanation:
Flags `:param:` fields in a reStructuredText docstring that are in a different order from the signature's parameters.
Readers match the fields against the signature from left to right, so a different order slows them down and hides a
missing field.

## Why is this bad?

A reader matches the documented parameters against the signature from left to right; a different order makes the
reference harder to scan and hides a missing field.

## Example

```toml config
[tool.simplint]
docstring-style = "rst"
```

```python report
def move(source: str, target: str) -> None:
    """Move a file.

    :param target: Where to.
    :param source: Where from.
    """
```

Use instead:

```python ok
def move(source: str, target: str) -> None:
    """Move a file.

    :param source: Where from.
    :param target: Where to.
    """
```

## Configuration

- [`docstring-style`](https://simplint.readthedocs.io/en/latest/configuration/rule-settings.html#docstring-markup) in
  `[tool.simplint]`: `"rst"` turns the rule on

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  def move(source: str, target: str) -> None:
      """Move a file.

      :param target: Where to.
      :param source: Where from.
      """
  ```

## What it does

Checks reStructuredText docstrings, when `docstring-style = "rst"`, for the order of their `:param:` fields. No fix is
offered, since moving fields can split the lines that continue them from their text.

### Active on

- **`:param:` fields for parameters the signature takes**: reported when their order differs from the signature's.

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  def move(source: str, target: str) -> None:
      """Move a file.

      :param target: Where to.
      :param source: Where from.
      """
  ```

### Exceptions

- **Fields for names the signature does not take**: these are left to [rst-unknown-param](SMP917.html), which reports
  them.

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python ok
  def move(source: str, target: str) -> None:
      """Move a file.

      :param gone: Removed.
      :param source: Where from.
      :param target: Where to.
      """
  ```

## Other tools

- **[Ruff](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff):** open pull request
  [#23047](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/23047) (DOC104) checks parameter order in Google and NumPy docstrings;
  reST fields are open issue [#12434](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/issues/12434).
- [pydoclint](https://github.com/jsh9/pydoclint) reports arguments documented in a different order than the signature as
  [DOC104](https://jsh9.github.io/pydoclint/violation_codes.html), with no fix.

name: rst-missing-attribute
summary: Public classes whose docstring leaves an attribute undocumented
explanation:
Flags attributes of a library's public classes that the reStructuredText class docstring leaves without an `:ivar:`,
`:cvar:` or `:var:` field. autodoc lists only documented attributes, so an undocumented one is invisible or unexplained
in the reference.

## Why is this bad?

Users read a class's attributes in the rendered reference, where autodoc lists only those with documentation. An
undocumented attribute is either invisible there or shown without saying what it holds.

## Example

```toml config
[tool.simplint]
docstring-style = "rst"
project-kind = "library"
```

```python report
class Engine:
    """Run jobs.

    :param speed: How fast it runs.
    """

    limit = 3

    def __init__(self, speed: int) -> None:
        self.speed = speed
        self.state = "idle"
```

Use instead:

```python ok
class Engine:
    """Run jobs.

    :param speed: How fast it runs.
    :cvar limit: The most jobs it runs at once.
    :ivar state: What it is doing.
    """
```

## Configuration

- [`docstring-style`](https://simplint.readthedocs.io/en/latest/configuration/rule-settings.html#docstring-markup) in
  `[tool.simplint]`: `"rst"` turns the rule on

  ```toml config
  [project]
  name = "demo"

  [build-system]
  requires = []

  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  class Engine:
      """Run jobs.

      :param speed: How fast it runs.
      """

      def __init__(self, speed: int) -> None:
          self.speed = speed
          self.state = "idle"
  ```

## What it does

Checks the docstrings of a library's public classes (see [undocumented-public-api](SMP903.html)), when
`docstring-style = "rst"`, for attributes without an `:ivar name:`, `:cvar name:` or `:var name:` field. The attributes
are those [autodoc](https://www.sphinx-doc.org/en/master/usage/extensions/autodoc.html) documents.

No fix is offered: the description is for the author to write, and [rst-empty-field](SMP914.html) reports the empty
field until they do.

### Active on

- **Names the class body assigns**: a `ClassVar` or a name assigned without an annotation is a class variable; an
  annotated name, such as a dataclass field, is an instance attribute; a class variable a method also sets on `self` is
  an instance attribute with a default.

  ```toml config
  [project]
  name = "demo"

  [build-system]
  requires = []

  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  class Engine:
      """Run jobs."""

      limit = 3
      state: str
  ```

- **Loop variables of the class body**: the target of a `for` statement in the class body is a class variable, as a name
  the body assigns without an annotation is, so the class documents it.

  ```toml config
  [project]
  name = "demo"

  [build-system]
  requires = []

  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  class Engine:
      """Run jobs."""

      for step in (1, 2):
          pass
  ```

- **Attributes a regular method sets on its first parameter**: these are instance attributes. A method sets them at any
  depth of its body, directly or through `object.__setattr__(self, "name", value)` as a frozen dataclass does. A class
  defined inside a method has its own `self`, so its attributes belong to that class instead.

  ```toml config
  [project]
  name = "demo"

  [build-system]
  requires = []

  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  class Engine:
      """Run jobs.

      :param speed: How fast it runs.
      """

      def __init__(self, speed: int) -> None:
          self.speed = speed
          self.state = "idle"
  ```

- **Attributes a class method sets on its first parameter**: these are class variables, found the same way.

  ```toml config
  [project]
  name = "demo"

  [build-system]
  requires = []

  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  class Engine:
      """Run jobs."""

      @classmethod
      def configure(cls) -> None:
          cls.limit = 3
  ```

### Exceptions

- **Names starting with `_`**: a leading underscore marks the name as internal, and [rst-private-field](SMP915.html)
  reports documentation of internal names in the public API.

  ```toml config
  [project]
  name = "demo"

  [build-system]
  requires = []

  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python ok
  class Engine:
      """Run jobs."""

      _cache = {}
  ```

- **Attributes documented in place**: a `#:` comment above the attribute, or a string right after it, documents it in
  the forms autodoc reads.

  ```toml config
  [project]
  name = "demo"

  [build-system]
  requires = []

  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python ok
  class Engine:
      """Run jobs."""

      #: The most jobs it runs at once.
      limit = 3

      rate = 2
      """Jobs started per second."""
  ```

- **Attributes the constructor takes as a parameter of the same name**: the `:param:` field documents it, which
  [rst-missing-param](SMP916.html) asks for.

  ```toml config
  [project]
  name = "demo"

  [build-system]
  requires = []

  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python ok
  class Engine:
      """Run jobs.

      :param speed: How fast it runs.
      """

      def __init__(self, speed: int) -> None:
          self.speed = speed
  ```

## Other tools

- **[Ruff](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff):** open issue [#12434](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/issues/12434).
- [pydoclint](https://github.com/jsh9/pydoclint) reports a class docstring that lists fewer attributes than the class
  has as [DOC601](https://jsh9.github.io/pydoclint/violation_codes.html), with no fix.

name: rst-unknown-attribute
summary: `:ivar:`, `:cvar:` and `:var:` fields for attributes the class lacks
explanation:
Flags `:ivar:`, `:cvar:`, `:var:` and `:vartype:` fields in a reStructuredText class docstring that name an attribute
the class does not have. Such a field, often left behind by a rename or removal, documents state no instance has.

## Why is this bad?

A field for an attribute that is gone, often renamed or removed in a later change, documents state no instance has.

## Example

```toml config
[tool.simplint]
docstring-style = "rst"
```

```python report
class Engine:
    """Run jobs.

    :ivar state: What it is doing.
    :ivar queue: The jobs waiting.
    """

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.state = "idle"
```

Use instead:

```python ok
class Engine:
    """Run jobs.

    :ivar state: What it is doing.
    """

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.state = "idle"
```

## Configuration

- [`docstring-style`](https://simplint.readthedocs.io/en/latest/configuration/rule-settings.html#docstring-markup) in
  `[tool.simplint]`: `"rst"` turns the rule on

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  class Engine:
      """Run jobs.

      :cvar limit: The most jobs it runs at once.
      """

      state = "idle"
  ```

## What it does

Checks the docstrings of classes, when `docstring-style = "rst"`, for `:ivar name:`, `:cvar name:`, `:var name:` and
`:vartype name:` fields naming an attribute the class does not have.

### Active on

- **Attribute fields in a class docstring**: reported when the name is none of the attributes the class has: those its
  body assigns, including names unpacked from a tuple and the strings of a `__slots__`, those its methods set on `self`,
  and its methods and properties, which autodoc can render as attributes.

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  class Engine:
      """Run jobs.

      :ivar state: What it is doing.
      :ivar queue: The jobs waiting.
      """

      def __init__(self) -> None:
          self.state = "idle"
  ```

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python ok
  class Engine:
      """Run jobs.

      :ivar run: The entry point.
      """

      def run(self) -> None:
          print()
  ```

- **Type aliases in the class body**: a `type` statement there is a class attribute, so a `:cvar` field may document it.

  ```toml config
  [project]
  requires-python = ">=3.12"

  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python ok
  class Engine:
      """Run jobs.

      :cvar Point: The pair of coordinates.
      """

      type Point = tuple[int, int]
  ```

### Exceptions

- **A class with a base class other than `object`, `ABC`, `Protocol`, `Generic`, `NamedTuple` or `TypedDict`**: the base
  may define the attribute.

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python ok
  class Engine(Base):
      """Run jobs.

      :ivar queue: The jobs waiting.
      """
  ```

- **Names a `__slots__` declares**: the strings of a string, tuple, list or set, and the keys of a dict, whether the
  assignment is annotated or not.

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python ok
  class Named:
      """A name.

      :ivar text: The text.
      """

      __slots__ = "text"


  class Pair:
      """Two names.

      :ivar first: The first.
      :ivar second: The second.
      """

      __slots__ = ("first", "second")


  class Listed:
      """A list of names.

      :ivar third: The third.
      """

      __slots__ = ["third"]


  class Stored:
      """A set of names.

      :ivar fourth: The fourth.
      """

      __slots__ = {"fourth"}


  class Keyed:
      """Keys.

      :ivar key: The key.
      """

      __slots__ = {"key": "The key."}


  class Annotated:
      """Annotated slots.

      :ivar size: The size.
      """

      __slots__: tuple[str, ...] = ("size",)
  ```

- **Names unpacked into the class body**: each name a tuple or starred target binds, such as `low` and `high` in
  `low, high = 0, 10`, or `tail` in `head, *tail = values`, and the target of a `for` statement in the class body.

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python ok
  class Bounds:
      """Limits of a range.

      :cvar low: The lower limit.
      :cvar high: The upper limit.
      :cvar tail: The rest.
      :cvar step: The distance between them.
      """

      low, high = 0, 10
      head, *tail = 1, 2, 3
      for step in (1, 2):
          pass
  ```

- **Members under `if` or `try` in the class body**: a method or assignment there is a member of the class, as one that
  a version check picks.

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python ok
  import sys


  class Engine:
      """Run jobs.

      :ivar run: The entry point.
      """

      if sys.version_info >= (3, 12):

          def run(self) -> None:
              print()

      else:

          def run(self) -> None:
              print()
  ```

### Fix

The fix deletes the field with the lines that continue it.

**Unsafe fix:** code may read the docstring through `__doc__`.

```toml config
[tool.simplint]
docstring-style = "rst"
```

```python report
class Engine:
    """Run jobs.

    :ivar state: What it is doing.
    :ivar queue: The jobs waiting.
    """

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.state = "idle"
```

```python fixed
class Engine:
    """Run jobs.

    :ivar state: What it is doing.
    """

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.state = "idle"
```

No fix is offered when escapes in the docstring make its text differ from the source.

## Other tools

- **[Ruff](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff):** open issue [#12434](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/issues/12434).
- [pydoclint](https://github.com/jsh9/pydoclint) reports a class docstring that lists more attributes than the class has
  as [DOC602](https://jsh9.github.io/pydoclint/violation_codes.html), with no fix.

name: rst-attribute-kind
summary: `:ivar:` on class variables and `:cvar:` on instance attributes
explanation:
Flags an `:ivar:` field documenting a class variable, or a `:cvar:` field documenting an instance attribute, in
reStructuredText class docstrings. Sphinx renders the two under different headings, so the wrong field sends readers to
the wrong place.

## Why is this bad?

Sphinx renders the two as "Instance Variables" and "Class Variables", so the wrong one tells readers to look for the
value in the wrong place.

## Example

```toml config
[tool.simplint]
docstring-style = "rst"
```

```python report
class Engine:
    """Run jobs.

    :ivar limit: The most jobs it runs at once.
    """

    limit = 3
```

Use instead:

```python ok
class Engine:
    """Run jobs.

    :cvar limit: The most jobs it runs at once.
    """

    limit = 3
```

## Configuration

- [`docstring-style`](https://simplint.readthedocs.io/en/latest/configuration/rule-settings.html#docstring-markup) in
  `[tool.simplint]`: `"rst"` turns the rule on

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  class Engine:
      """Run jobs.

      :ivar limit: The most jobs it runs at once.
      """

      limit = 3
  ```

## What it does

Checks the docstrings of classes, when `docstring-style = "rst"`, for attribute fields of the wrong kind.

### Active on

- **`:ivar name:` fields**: reported when `name` is a class variable.

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  class Engine:
      """Run jobs.

      :ivar limit: The most jobs it runs at once.
      """

      limit = 3
  ```

  A `ClassVar` annotation counts the same when quoted, as `"ClassVar[int]"`.

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  from typing import ClassVar


  class Engine:
      """Run jobs.

      :ivar limit: The most jobs it runs at once.
      """

      limit: "ClassVar[int]" = 3
  ```

- **A loop variable of the class body**: the target of a `for` statement there is a class variable, so `:ivar:` for it
  is reported.

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  class Engine:
      """Run jobs.

      :ivar step: The step.
      """

      for step in (1, 2):
          pass
  ```

- **`:cvar name:` fields**: reported when `name` is an instance attribute.

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  class Engine:
      """Run jobs.

      :cvar state: What it is doing.
      """

      def __init__(self) -> None:
          self.state = "idle"
  ```

### Exceptions

- **`:var name:` fields**: `:var:` suits both kinds.

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python ok
  class Engine:
      """Run jobs.

      :var limit: The most jobs it runs at once.
      """

      limit = 3
  ```

- **A class default that methods also set on `self`**: the attribute is both kinds, so `:ivar:` and `:cvar:` both fit.

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python ok
  class Engine:
      """Run jobs.

      :ivar limit: The most jobs it runs at once.
      """

      limit = 3

      def reset(self) -> None:
          self.limit = 3
  ```

### Attribute kinds

| Attribute                                                                          | Kind               | Field                |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------ | -------------------- |
| a `ClassVar`                                                                       | class variable     | `:cvar:`             |
| a `Final` with a value in the class body, as `SHOW: Final = 1`                     | class variable     | `:cvar:`             |
| a name the class body assigns without an annotation, that no method sets on `self` | class variable     | `:cvar:`             |
| the target of a `for` statement in the class body                                  | class variable     | `:cvar:`             |
| an annotated field                                                                 | instance attribute | `:ivar:`             |
| a name a method sets on `self`                                                     | instance attribute | `:ivar:`             |
| a class default that methods also set on `self`                                    | both               | `:ivar:` or `:cvar:` |

### Fix

The fix renames the field, keeping its description.

**Unsafe fix:** code may read the docstring through `__doc__`.

```toml config
[tool.simplint]
docstring-style = "rst"
```

```python report
class Engine:
    """Run jobs.

    :ivar limit: The most jobs it runs at once.
    """

    limit = 3
```

```python fixed
class Engine:
    """Run jobs.

    :cvar limit: The most jobs it runs at once.
    """

    limit = 3
```

No fix is offered when escapes in the docstring make its text differ from the source.

## Other tools

- **[Ruff](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff):** not requested yet.

name: rst-returns
summary: Missing, extraneous or misused `:returns:` and `:yields:` fields
explanation:
Flags missing, extraneous and misused `:returns:` and `:yields:` fields in reStructuredText docstrings. What a function
hands back is half of its contract, so a missing field leaves it unsaid and a wrong one describes a value no caller
receives.

## Why is this bad?

What a function hands back is half of its contract. A missing field leaves it to the annotation alone; a `:returns:` on
a function that returns nothing, or on a generator, describes a value no caller receives.

## Example

```toml config
[tool.simplint]
docstring-style = "rst"
project-kind = "library"
```

```python report
def total(values: list[int]) -> int:
    """Add the values.

    :param values: The values.
    """
    return sum(values)
```

Use instead:

```python ok
def total(values: list[int]) -> int:
    """Add the values.

    :param values: The values.
    :returns: Their sum.
    """
    return sum(values)
```

## Conflicts with Ruff

Ruff's [docstring-missing-returns](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/docstring-missing-returns/) and
[docstring-missing-yields](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/docstring-missing-yields/) read Google and numpydoc
sections only, so they report the `:returns:` and `:yields:` fields this rule asks for as missing sections. simplint
stops with an error before linting while either applies to a file this rule checks; turn them off in Ruff, or turn this
rule off.

## Configuration

- [`docstring-style`](https://simplint.readthedocs.io/en/latest/configuration/rule-settings.html#docstring-markup) in
  `[tool.simplint]`: `"rst"` turns the rule on

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  def total(values: list[int]) -> int:
      """Add the values.

      :param values: The values.
      :yields: Each value.
      """
      return sum(values)
  ```

## What it does

Checks the `:returns:` and `:yields:` fields of reStructuredText docstrings, when `docstring-style = "rst"`. A
**missing** field is reported in a docstring of a library's public API (see [undocumented-public-api](SMP903.html)); a
**wrong** field is reported in any docstring.

### Active on

- **Public functions that return a value without a `:returns:` field**: the return annotation is not `None`, `NoReturn`
  or `Never`, or, without one, the function returns something other than `None`. No fix is offered: the description is
  for the author to write, and [rst-empty-field](SMP914.html) reports an empty `:returns:` until they do.

  ```toml config
  [project]
  name = "demo"

  [build-system]
  requires = []

  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  def total(values: list[int]) -> int:
      """Add the values.

      :param values: The values.
      """
      return sum(values)
  ```

- **Public generators without a `:yields:` field**: no fix is offered, for the same reason.

  ```toml config
  [project]
  name = "demo"

  [build-system]
  requires = []

  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  def numbers(count: int):
      """Count up.

      :param count: How far.
      """
      yield from range(count)
  ```

- **`:returns:` on a function that returns nothing**: its annotation says so, or, without one, it has no `return` with a
  value and its body is more than a placeholder such as `...`, as in an abstract method. The fix deletes the `:returns:`
  and `:rtype:` fields with the lines that continue them.

  ```toml config
  [project]
  name = "demo"

  [build-system]
  requires = []

  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  def log(message: str) -> None:
      """Write the message.

      :param message: The text.
      :returns: Nothing.
      """
      print(message)
  ```

  ```python fixed
  def log(message: str) -> None:
      """Write the message.

      :param message: The text.
      """
      print(message)
  ```

  A quoted annotation, such as `-> "None"`, counts the same as its unquoted form:

  ```toml config
  [project]
  name = "demo"

  [build-system]
  requires = []

  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  def log(message: str) -> "None":
      """Write the message.

      :param message: The text.
      :returns: Nothing.
      """
      print(message)
  ```

- **`:returns:` and no `:yields:` on a generator**: the fix renames the field to `:yields:`, keeping its description.

  ```toml config
  [project]
  name = "demo"

  [build-system]
  requires = []

  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  def numbers(count: int):
      """Count up.

      :param count: How far.
      :returns: Each number.
      """
      yield from range(count)
  ```

  ```python fixed
  def numbers(count: int):
      """Count up.

      :param count: How far.
      :yields: Each number.
      """
      yield from range(count)
  ```

- **`:yields:` on a function that is not a generator**: the fix deletes the `:yields:` and `:ytype:` fields.

  ```toml config
  [project]
  name = "demo"

  [build-system]
  requires = []

  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  def total(values: list[int]) -> int:
      """Add the values.

      :param values: The values.
      :returns: The sum.
      :yields: Each value.
      """
      return sum(values)
  ```

  ```python fixed
  def total(values: list[int]) -> int:
      """Add the values.

      :param values: The values.
      :returns: The sum.
      """
      return sum(values)
  ```

- **A `:returns:`, `:rtype:`, `:yields:` or `:ytype:` field in the docstring of a class or a property**: no fix is
  offered, since that text belongs in the description, and moving it there is for the author.

  - The docstring of a class, which describes the class

    ```toml config
    [project]
    name = "demo"

    [build-system]
    requires = []

    [tool.simplint]
    docstring-style = "rst"
    ```

    ```python report
    class Engine:
        """Run jobs.

        :returns: The engine.
        """
    ```

  - The docstring of a property, whose text describes the value it holds

    ```toml config
    [project]
    name = "demo"

    [build-system]
    requires = []

    [tool.simplint]
    docstring-style = "rst"
    ```

    ```python report
    class Engine:
        """Run jobs."""

        @property
        def speed(self) -> int:
            """The speed.

            :returns: Units per second.
            """
            return 1
    ```

### Exceptions

- **`__init__`**: a constructor returns nothing to document.

  ```toml config
  [project]
  name = "demo"

  [build-system]
  requires = []

  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python ok
  class Engine:
      """Run jobs."""

      def __init__(self, speed: int) -> None:
          """Set up.

          :param speed: How fast it runs.
          """
          self.speed = speed
  ```

- **A `yield` inside a lambda**: the lambda is a generator of its own, so the function around it is not one.

  ```toml config
  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python ok
  def count(values: list[int]) -> int:
      """Count the values.

      :param values: The inputs.
      :returns: How many there are.
      """
      probe = lambda: (yield)  # noqa: E731
      return len(values) + bool(probe)
  ```

- **A body that is only a placeholder**: a body such as `...`, `pass` or `raise NotImplementedError`, as in an abstract
  method, says nothing of the return or the yields, so neither a missing `:returns:` nor a `:yields:` is reported for
  it.

  ```toml config
  [project]
  name = "demo"

  [build-system]
  requires = []

  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python ok file=total.py
  def total(values: list[int]):
      """Add the values.

      :param values: The values.
      """
      ...
  ```

  ```python ok file=rows.py
  from collections.abc import Iterator


  def rows() -> Iterator[str]:
      """Read the rows.

      :yields: Each row.
      """
      ...
  ```

### Fix

**Unsafe fix:** each fix changes the docstring, and code may read it through `__doc__`.

No fix is offered when escapes in the docstring make its text differ from the source.

## Other tools

- **[Ruff](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff):** variation of preview rules
  [DOC201](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/docstring-missing-returns/) and
  [DOC402](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/docstring-missing-yields/), which cannot read `:returns:` and `:yields:`
  fields, so simplint refuses to run with them on reST docstrings; open pull request
  [#13286](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/13286) adds Sphinx support.
- [pydoclint](https://github.com/jsh9/pydoclint) reports missing or extra return and yield sections as
  [DOC201](https://jsh9.github.io/pydoclint/violation_codes.html),
  [DOC202](https://jsh9.github.io/pydoclint/violation_codes.html),
  [DOC402](https://jsh9.github.io/pydoclint/violation_codes.html) and
  [DOC403](https://jsh9.github.io/pydoclint/violation_codes.html), with no fix.
- [darglint](https://github.com/terrencepreilly/darglint) reports the same return sections as
  [DAR201](https://github.com/terrencepreilly/darglint) and [DAR202](https://github.com/terrencepreilly/darglint), with
  no fix.

name: rst-missing-raises
summary: Public API docstrings that leave a raised exception undocumented
explanation:
Flags exceptions a public API function raises itself that its reStructuredText docstring leaves without a
`:raises Error:` field. Callers handle the exceptions they know about, so an undocumented one reaches them as a
surprise.

## Why is this bad?

Callers handle the exceptions they know about. One the docstring leaves out reaches them as a surprise, often in
production, where the error path is first exercised.

## Example

```toml config
[tool.simplint]
docstring-style = "rst"
project-kind = "library"
```

```python report
def parse(text: str) -> int:
    """Parse a number.

    :param text: The text.
    :returns: The number.
    """
    if not text:
        raise ValueError("empty")
    return int(text)
```

Use instead:

```python ok
def parse(text: str) -> int:
    """Parse a number.

    :param text: The text.
    :returns: The number.
    :raises ValueError: When the text is empty.
    """
    if not text:
        raise ValueError("empty")
    return int(text)
```

## Conflicts with Ruff

Ruff's [docstring-missing-exception](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/docstring-missing-exception/) reads Google and
numpydoc sections only, so it reports the `:raises:` fields this rule asks for as a missing section. simplint stops with
an error before linting while it applies to a file this rule checks; turn it off in Ruff, or turn this rule off.

## Configuration

- [`docstring-style`](https://simplint.readthedocs.io/en/latest/configuration/rule-settings.html#docstring-markup) in
  `[tool.simplint]`: `"rst"` turns the rule on

  ```toml config
  [project]
  name = "demo"

  [build-system]
  requires = []

  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  def parse(text: str) -> int:
      """Parse a number.

      :param text: The text.
      :returns: The number.
      """
      if not text:
          raise ValueError("empty")
      return int(text)
  ```

## What it does

Checks the docstrings of a library's public API (see [undocumented-public-api](SMP903.html)), when
`docstring-style = "rst"`, for exceptions the function raises itself without a `:raises Error:` field.

No fix is offered: the description is for the author to write, and [rst-empty-field](SMP914.html) reports the empty
field until they do.

### Active on

- **`raise` statements that name an exception class**: each exception the function raises by name and lets escape needs
  a field. A field matches by the exception's last name, so `:raises errors.ParseError:` documents
  `raise errors.ParseError(...)`.

  ```toml config
  [project]
  name = "demo"

  [build-system]
  requires = []

  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  import errors


  def parse(text: str) -> int:
      """Parse a number.

      :param text: The text.
      :returns: The number.
      """
      raise errors.ParseError(text)
  ```

### Exceptions

- **A bare `raise`, and a `raise` of an exception the function caught, as `raise error` in `except ... as error`**:
  these re-raise an exception that came from elsewhere rather than naming one.

  - A bare `raise` in an `except` block

    ```toml config
    [project]
    name = "demo"

    [build-system]
    requires = []

    [tool.simplint]
    docstring-style = "rst"
    ```

    ```python ok
    def parse(text: str) -> int:
        """Parse a number.

        :param text: The text.
        :returns: The number.
        """
        try:
            return int(text)
        except ValueError:
            raise
    ```

  - A `raise error` of the exception that `except ValueError as error` caught

    ```toml config
    [project]
    name = "demo"

    [build-system]
    requires = []

    [tool.simplint]
    docstring-style = "rst"
    ```

    ```python ok
    def parse(text: str) -> int:
        """Parse a number.

        :param text: The text.
        :returns: The number.
        """
        try:
            return int(text)
        except ValueError as error:
            raise error
    ```

- **An exception a surrounding `try` of the same function catches**: it does not escape the function. The `try` catches
  it by name, through a built-in base such as `OSError` for `FileNotFoundError`, through `Exception`, which does not
  catch `SystemExit`, `KeyboardInterrupt` or `GeneratorExit`, or through `BaseException`.

  ```toml config
  [project]
  name = "demo"

  [build-system]
  requires = []

  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python ok
  def read(path: str) -> str:
      """Read a file.

      :param path: Where it is.
      :returns: The text.
      """
      try:
          raise FileNotFoundError(path)
      except OSError:
          return ""
  ```

  ```toml config
  [project]
  name = "demo"

  [build-system]
  requires = []

  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python report
  def stop(code: int) -> int:
      """Stop the job.

      :param code: The exit code.
      :returns: Nothing.
      """
      try:
          raise SystemExit(code)
      except Exception:
          return 0
  ```

- **An exception whose built-in base a field documents**: a field for the base documents its subclasses too, as
  `:raises OSError:` does `FileNotFoundError`.

  ```toml config
  [project]
  name = "demo"

  [build-system]
  requires = []

  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python ok
  def read(path: str) -> str:
      """Read a file.

      :param path: Where it is.
      :raises OSError: When the file cannot be read.
      :returns: The text.
      """
      raise FileNotFoundError(path)
  ```

- **`NotImplementedError`**: it marks a method for subclasses to override.

  ```toml config
  [project]
  name = "demo"

  [build-system]
  requires = []

  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python ok
  def run() -> None:
      """Run the job."""
      raise NotImplementedError
  ```

- **A `raise` inside a nested function or class**: it runs when the nested function or class does, not as part of this
  function's body.

  ```toml config
  [project]
  name = "demo"

  [build-system]
  requires = []

  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python ok
  def make() -> object:
      """Make a callback.

      :returns: The callback.
      """

      def callback() -> None:
          raise ValueError("later")

      return callback
  ```

- **A name starting in lowercase**: it is a variable rather than an exception class.

  ```toml config
  [project]
  name = "demo"

  [build-system]
  requires = []

  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python ok
  def run(problem: Exception) -> None:
      """Run the job.

      :param problem: What to raise.
      """
      raise problem
  ```

- **Exceptions raised by the functions it calls**: the code does not show them.

  ```toml config
  [project]
  name = "demo"

  [build-system]
  requires = []

  [tool.simplint]
  docstring-style = "rst"
  ```

  ```python ok
  def run() -> None:
      """Run the job."""
      load()
  ```

The bases of built-in exceptions are known; those of a project's own exceptions are not.

## Other tools

- **[Ruff](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff):** variation of preview rule
  [DOC501](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/docstring-missing-exception/), which cannot read `:raises:` fields, so
  simplint refuses to run with it on reST docstrings; open pull request
  [#13286](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/13286) adds Sphinx support.
- [pydoclint](https://github.com/jsh9/pydoclint) reports raised exceptions missing from or extra in the docstring as
  [DOC501](https://jsh9.github.io/pydoclint/violation_codes.html) and
  [DOC502](https://jsh9.github.io/pydoclint/violation_codes.html), with no fix.
- [darglint](https://github.com/terrencepreilly/darglint) reports the same exceptions as
  [DAR401](https://github.com/terrencepreilly/darglint) and [DAR402](https://github.com/terrencepreilly/darglint), with
  no fix.

blocks.source:
import errors


def parse(text: str) -> int:
    """Parse a number.

    :param text: The text.
    :returns: The number.
    """
    raise errors.ParseError(text)

def read(path: str) -> str:
    """Read a file.

    :param path: Where it is.
    :raises OSError: When the file cannot be read.
    :returns: The text.
    """
    raise FileNotFoundError(path)

def make() -> object:
    """Make a callback.

    :returns: The callback.
    """

    def callback() -> None:
        raise ValueError("later")

    return callback

def run(problem: Exception) -> None:
    """Run the job.

    :param problem: What to raise.
    """
    raise problem
